A technique to perform single-view reconstruction by optimizing the periodic activation parameters (frequencies and phase shifts) of a frozen implicit radiance field generator to match a target image, without modifying the network weights [S2].

The claim accurately summarizes the method described in Source [S2]. The source explicitly states that they freeze the parameters of the implicit representation (network weights) and optimize the frequencies (γi) and phase shifts (βi) to match a target image. It details the initialization using the center of mass from 10,000 random noise vectors, the use of gradient descent with an L2 penalty (weight 0.1), and the specific Adam optimizer settings (700 iterations, initial LR 0.01, decay factor 0.5 every 200 iterations). All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
